summary.headline: Veranda Q2 FY27 continuing-business revenue rose 17% YoY to INR51 crores; EBITDA up 28% to INR12.7 crores after commerce demerger.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 is the first quarter reported on a continuing-business basis, with the commerce business (now J.K. Shah Commerce Education) demerged effective 1 September 2026. Revenue from operations rose 17% YoY to INR51 crores and government test prep grew 31% YoY, while EBITDA rose 28% YoY to INR12.7 crores at a 25% margin. Finance costs fell 58% YoY to INR4.8 crores, turning PAT to INR13.4 crores from a loss of INR12.8 crores a year earlier. Reported consolidated numbers include a one-time exceptional fair-value gain of INR1,047 crores on the demerger, which management said does not affect reserves. FY27 continuing-business guidance was reiterated at INR175 crores revenue, INR46 crores EBITDA and about INR32 crores PAT.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 31% YoY in Q2, with EBITDA up 79% per analyst's question; drivers were fee increases of 7-10% YoY, higher utilisation of existing centres, and new Junior IAS, Group 1 and subscription programmes. Over 40 centres across South India.

segments.name: Academics / K-12 (books and schools)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue dipped QoQ because Q1 is admission season with book sales; H1 revenue grew 12% from INR17 crores to INR19 crores and EBITDA from INR11 crores to INR15 crores. Managed schools: 6 schools with over 5,400 students on an asset-light model; no new schools added except one international school in the last couple of years.

segments.name: SNVA Veranda (associate)
segments.commentary: Veranda holds about 40% stake; business is online university partnerships in the US and EU, a physical campus in Lyon and a planned Dubai campus. Management said a listing is targeted in the near future, but no definitive milestone is yet announced.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing-business guidance intact: revenue INR175 crores, EBITDA INR46 crores, PAT about INR32 crores.
Long-term target: revenue of INR600 crores in about five years and EBITDA of INR120-140 crores (from current INR45 crores run-rate), per management.
Sustainable EBITDA margin for continuing business seen at 23-25%.
Managed schools target scaled to more than 30 schools in the next few years; preschool entry under Veranda Sprouts this year.

Karnataka: first centre in Mysore opened; plan of 4 centres this year and 4 next year; 30-35% CAGR expected; long-term EBITDA target of INR20-25 crores in about 4-5 years, comparable to Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
Management plans to reinvest all non-commerce free cash flow; dividend from the non-commerce business not indicated. Commerce (J.K. Shah) dividend to be considered by its own board.
capex_capacity: Karnataka centre capex (interiors, rental deposit and fit-out) about INR30-35 lakh per centre.
Growth is mainly from higher utilisation of existing centres without new capacity, which management credited for margin gains.
Plan to add managed schools and the preschool segment; the new K-12 curriculum (Class 1-12) was introduced over the last 6-7 months.
Finance costs reduced after deleveraging; cost of borrowing cut from about 17% to about 9%.
demand_pricing: Government test prep demand is strong; enrolments grew 12% in H1 and collections rose 17%.
Management says fees rise 7-10% YoY while costs rise about 4% YoY.
Private equity entry into premium K-12 is seen as healthy for valuations and as creating aggregation opportunities for smaller schools; management sees some competition in pockets.

qa_highlights.question: Why is academics flat or down QoQ while test prep grows 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is admission season with book sales, so the Q2 dip is seasonal; H1 academics revenue grew 12% to INR19 crores and EBITDA rose from INR11 crores to INR15 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What drove test prep EBITDA growth of 79% against revenue growth of 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee increases of 7-10%, costs rising about 4%, higher utilisation of existing capacity without new centres, and new programmes like Junior IAS and expanded UPSC batches.

qa_highlights.question: How many schools were added in the last three years and what are the plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Except one international school, no new schools were added; the first year after acquisition went to stabilising systems and phasing out promoters, and management now plans to add schools via management partnerships and enter preschool.

qa_highlights.question: How should Karnataka expansion economics be evaluated and what is capex per centre?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 centres planned this year and 4 next year, targeting 30-35% CAGR and EBITDA of INR20-25 crores over 4-5 years; capex per centre INR30-35 lakh including interiors and deposit.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the demerger accounted as fair value and not common control, and what does the INR1,047 crore gain mean for book value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no single shareholder holds more than 51%, so it is not common control and is accounted under Ind AS 10 as fair value. The gain goes through retained earnings and the reserves movement is nil, so net worth stays near INR500-518 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SNVA Veranda listing status?
qa_highlights.answer: A listing is the target in the near future, not the distant future; management is working on options and expects to announce definitive milestones in the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Commerce (J.K. Shah) listing timing and price; management expects a significant value move but gave no figures. Shareholder value depends on that listing.
Dividend: no payout planned for the non-commerce business; management will refer dividend questions on J.K. Shah to its board.
Academics growth is seasonal, so Q3 and Q4 need to show the H1 trend holding up.
Managed schools: little new school addition in the last three years; the 30-school target depends on execution.
Karnataka ramp-up and new-centre costs could pressure margins; management says existing programmes will offset them.
Book value and consolidated accounting treatment of the INR1,047 crore exceptional gain; an analyst questioned the figure and management's answer was partly unclear.
Attention needed on the SNVA Veranda listing and the associate stake value.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and deleveraging, with a clear focus on the continuing businesses. Management was evasive on dividends, the J.K. Shah valuation and the SNVA listing timing, and on the INR1,047 crore accounting, which it explained only partly.
key_quotes: So the preschool segment is also being entered into with a very clear defined methodical planning.
So a lot of groundwork has happened basis which we expect to be able to grow in the coming years.
So we are seeing a strong 30% to 35% CAGR, which we are expecting to grow in that business.

adds.what: Karnataka test-prep centres: first Mysore centre opened; plan of 4 more this year and 4 next year
Managed schools and preschool (Veranda Sprouts) additions planned; target of more than 30 managed schools in next few years

growth.why: FY27 continuing-business guidance reiterated at INR175 crore revenue, INR46 crore EBITDA and about INR32 crore PAT, which implies a strong H2 given H1 revenue of INR104 crore; backing is partial, with fee increases of 7-10%, enrolments up 12% in H1, and Karnataka centres (4 this year), but no firm capacity schedule for the core business, which grows mainly from utilisation of existing centres.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 25% (Q1 23%) and management sees sustainable 23-25%; fee hikes of 7-10% vs cost growth about 4% and lower ad spend drive operating leverage.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First Mysore Karnataka centre opened, with 4 more planned this year and 4 next year at INR30-35 lakh capex each; managed schools and Veranda Sprouts preschool also planned, though the core growth is from existing centre utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Government test prep revenue up 31% YoY in Q2 and enrolments up 12% in H1; H1 continuing revenue INR104 crore vs INR175 crore FY27 guide implies a strong H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation level was not disclosed and no new major plant is planned; capex is limited to Karnataka centre fit-outs (INR30-35 lakh each) and school additions, so a larger capex call is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance reiterated at INR175 crore revenue, INR46 crore EBITDA and about INR32 crore PAT, not raised, despite H1 revenue of INR104 crore; the call gave no sign of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Karnataka ramp-up and new-centre costs could pressure margins, and academics is seasonal so Q3-Q4 must hold the H1 trend to meet the INR175 crore revenue guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Veranda Sprouts preschool entry this year and the new K-12 curriculum (Class 1-12) rolled out over the last 6-7 months; new test-prep programmes (Junior IAS, Group 1, subscriptions) already launched.

rows.label: SNVA Veranda listing (associate ~40% stake)
rows.why: Management targets a listing in the near future and expects definitive milestones in the next couple of quarters, but no date or figures are yet announced.

rows.label: J.K. Shah Commerce listing and value unlock
rows.why: Management expects a significant value move on listing but gave no timing or figures; commerce FY27 PAT guide about INR110 crore is discontinued from continuing numbers.

rows.label: Lower finance costs after deleveraging
rows.why: Finance costs fell 58% YoY to INR4.8 crore from INR11.5 crore, with borrowing cost cut from about 17% to about 9%.

tone.note: Management was confident on test-prep growth, margins, deleveraging and Karnataka expansion, but evasive on dividends, the J.K. Shah valuation, SNVA listing timing and the INR1,047 crore accounting; analysts pushed on the EBITDA-revenue gap, academics seasonality and the accounting treatment.
